key_insight: A training-free pipeline enables rich, controllable edits of video content, actions, and dynamics — including inserting new actors or events that influence other objects — by leveraging pretrained generative priors and motion-aware, inference-time optimization. This removes the need for task-specific training data while supporting non‑structure-preserving edits.
problem_solved: How to perform complex, behaviorally consistent edits (change actions, dynamics, or insert content that affects other objects) in real-world videos without collecting large, specialized training datasets or fine-tuning models.
method: Use pretrained generative/video priors at inference time (no additional training) to synthesize plausible appearance and motion for edits.
Decompose video into object- and motion-centric components and apply motion-aware constraints (flow/temporal consistency, object interactions) so edits affect scene dynamics coherently.
Optimize edit parameters at test-time with compositional control (spatial masks, action descriptors, temporal anchors) to insert or modify content that interacts naturally with existing elements.
impact: Provides a practical toolset for flexible, high-fidelity video editing without costly dataset collection or retraining, enabling rapid prototyping and creative workflows for researchers and practitioners in video synthesis and content creation.
visual_elements: Before/after video strip showing an inserted actor whose motion alters nearby objects (demonstrates behavioral coupling).
Pipeline diagram: input video → object/motion decomposition → pretrained prior + inference optimization → edited video.
Visualization of motion constraints: optical flow overlays or trajectories showing temporal coherence.
Comparison panel: training-free edits vs. trained-model failures (highlighting generalization and fidelity differences).
paper_title: Versatile Editing of Video Content, Actions, and Dynamics without Training
paper_authors: Vladimir Kulikov, Roni Paiss, Andrey Voynov, Inbar Mosseri, Tali Dekel
